newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia won't extend deadline for illegal workers.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia won't extend deadline for illegal workers.

text.p: Malaysia will not extend the December 31, 1996 registration deadline for illegal foreign workers, the national Bernama news agency reported on Wednesday.

"The government has repeatedly stated that although emphasis is given on economic growth, we cannot compromise on matters which affect the security of the country," Deputy Home Minister Ong Ka Ting told reporters.
Malaysian police, immigration and army personnel are expected to launch a nationwide operation to catch and deport illegal immigrants from January after the amnesty period ends.

During the legalisation exercise, about 300,000 foreign workers were registered by their employers, Bernama quoted Ong as saying. Malaysia, with a population of about 20 million, has an estimated one million illegal workers.

Under the Immigration Act, employers who employ a foreign worker without permit can be fined up to 10,000 ringgit ($3,968) or jailed for five years. Those employing more then five illegal foreign workers are liable to a mandatory jail term of up to six months.
Foreign workers who have been registered cannot switch jobs and will be deemed as being without work permits if they do so, Ong said.
Malaysia's booming economy has created acute labour shortages and provided a magnet for foreign workers.
